title: Reinforcement Learning without Verifiable Rewards — Will Brown, Prime Intellect
talk_summary: Will Brown describes how to manufacture training/eval signal when rewards aren't verifiable: grounding against source material, LLM judges, working backwards from known-good end states, and scaling test-time compute to mine traces and build rubrics. The core loop is turning production traces and completed artifacts into tasks, then spending inference compute to grade and refine them.

takeaways.technique: Work backwards from known-good end states
takeaways.what_they_do: Take a completed artifact (a merged PR, a fixed bug) and remove pieces to create a task whose end state is known reachable, then have agents replay to rediscover it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: take something that is a completed artifact and start breaking it down into smaller pieces and then have replaying these pieces

takeaways.what_they_do: After a rollout, spend compute having multiple models look back at the trace to identify what went wrong, then distill those into reusable rubric questions for cheaper auditing.
Treat deployed agent traces (user prompts, orchestrator-to-subagent calls) as the distribution to learn from even without labels, then generate tasks grounded in them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: taking existing traces from a deployed agent and treating these as the source material

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate tasks, solve them, and gate on pass rate so tasks are neither too easy nor too hard, then train/eval on the calibrated set.
takeaways.evidence_quote: gating based on this pass rate which then we train on and we see a great uplift

takeaways.what_they_do: Collect examples of reward hacks over time and use adversarial prompt optimization to probe for backdoors, then refine the reward/verifier implementation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: building up your corpus of examples of reward hacks, you can understand the sorts of things that go wrong

takeaways.technique: Simulators with controllable backends for verification
takeaways.what_they_do: Build high-fidelity simulators of tools/web apps where you control backend state, so you can plant the answer and verify outcomes even when production isn't verifiable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have full controllability over the back-end ... you get to kind of plant the answer
